ei.subject: 영어Ⅰ
ei.title: The ABCs of Stocks and Stock Markets

fullPassage:
Neil: Welcome to the 10-Minute Economics 101 podcast for teenagers! I'm your host, Neil. Thank you for tuning in. We have a very special guest with us, the renowned economist Beth Friedman. Please give her a warm welcome!
Beth: Hello, everyone. It's truly an honor to be here with all of you.
Neil: We've been exploring the basics of economics. In this 35th episode, we'll be talking about the world of stocks. So let's get started.
Beth: Before we begin, Neil, I have a question for you. Have you ever wondered what to do with your extra money?
Neil: Absolutely, Beth. I bet all our listeners have asked themselves the same question.
Beth: Indeed. It's a question that often arises, especially among young people who are beginning to explore the world of finance. As you go about your daily lives, you find yourself engaged in financial activities such as purchasing goods and paying bus fares. After that, you might have some extra money.
Neil: You're right. Some people might save it in the bank, and others might prefer keeping it in their wallets for immediate use. There are also a few who have already been venturing into stock trading. Today, we're going to provide you with an overview of stocks and stock markets, enabling you to gain insight into the economy.
Beth: Okay, let's start with the concept of a stock. A stock is a partial share of ownership in a company. When you buy a stock, you get a portion of the company's ownership. To put it simply, owning one stock is like having a slice of the company's pie.
Neil: Does that mean stockholders themselves can actively participate in the management of the company?
Beth: Not exactly, Neil. Management is generally carried out by professional managers. However, companies hold stockholder meetings to seek the opinions of major stockholders when they make important decisions.
Neil: I see. Then how do companies use the stock market?
Beth: The stock market is very important for companies because it can provide them with the money they need to grow and expand.
Neil: How does that work?
Beth: Let's imagine that a small group of people start a footwear company producing innovative sneakers. The founders are confident that their products will be popular with consumers, but they do not have enough funds to grow the business. So they decide to put the newly formed company on the stock market.
Neil: What happens then?
Beth: When a company is listed on the stock market, individuals or organizations that believe in the company's bright future can buy shares and become partial owners of the company. This process makes it easy for the footwear company to raise the funds it needs to grow its business. As the business grows, the stock value rises, and the stockholders' profits increase.
Neil: Then what factors affect the prices of stocks?
Beth: Just like other transactions, the prices of stocks are decided by the law of supply and demand. In other words, the more successful a business is, the more people will see the potential value of the company and start buying its stocks. As demand for the stocks increases, so does the stock price. In contrast, if a company performs disappointingly, its stock price will fall.
Neil: Understood. Are there any other factors affecting the price?
Beth: Yes, companies are constantly under the influence of market factors such as raw material prices, advances in production technology, and labor costs. For example, in terms of raw material prices, if the price of rubber rises, a shoe company may have to pay more to import the rubber it needs from abroad to manufacture sneakers. This, in turn, affects production costs and leads to higher prices in the consumer market. As consumers hesitate to purchase the company's sneakers, the company may suffer from poor performance, leading to a decline in the stock price.
Neil: There are so many things to consider!
Beth: Additionally, investors may be concerned about a company's leadership or reputation. Nowadays, more and more people are starting to support companies that prioritize public values such as business transparency, environmental friendliness, and social justice. In purchasing such stocks, they not only pursue their financial goals but also contribute to building a more sustainable economic system that benefits the entire society. All these variables can cause daily changes in stock prices in the stock market.
Neil: It seems to get more difficult as we learn more about stocks. So how do we invest in the stock market?
Beth: You can buy stocks through an official place called a stock exchange, or stock market, where you can easily buy or sell stocks in a company. You might think investing in stocks is an easy way to make a profit. But if you are investing, you must be prepared to lose money. Since the market constantly fluctuates, there is a risk of loss and debt.
Neil: Investing in stocks is challenging! I bet our listeners are curious about the best investment options though.
Beth: That depends on individual circumstances. Generally, it would be smart to invest in something that interests you, such as a company behind some products you are into. Always remember to do your research, stay informed about the companies you invest in, and be mindful of your risk tolerance.
Neil: Investing can be a powerful tool for building wealth, but it's essential to approach it with knowledge and caution.
Beth: Wise words, Neil.
Neil: All right. I hope today's episode was helpful for you! I'll be back with another exciting topic next time, so make sure to tune in to 10-Minute Economics 101 again! If you found this episode helpful, please share it with any friends who might be interested in learning more about economics!

[Further Reading: Bull Market vs. Bear Market]
Stock market movement can be divided into two major trends: bull market vs. bear market.
A bull market is a rising stock market situation in which economic conditions are favorable to investors. They include high employment rates, GDP increases, and other positive economic indicators. Think of a charging bull in a field raising its horns. In a bull market, investors often believe in the market's present and future performance. As such, they increase their stock purchases and maintain their investments.
Like a standing bear having lowered its front legs, a bear market implies a decline in stock values. It occurs when economic conditions are not favorable, and most stocks experience decreases in value. Factors like low GDP growth, rising unemployment, and low wages are possible conditions for a bear market. In difficult economic situations, investors frequently have negative views of the stock market, which may lead them to sell their stocks.

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
Have you ever ______ what to do with your extra money?

det.ref:
[원문] Have you ever wondered what to do with your extra money?
[해석] 여분의 돈으로 무엇을 할지 궁금해 본 적이 있나요? [문장 04 참고]
det.correct: 현재완료 「have + p.p.」 구조이므로 과거분사 wondered가 정답입니다.
wrongs: ① wonder ❌ — 동사원형은 have 뒤에 올 수 없음
② wondered ✅ — have + p.p. 구조에 적합
③ wondering ❌ — 현재분사는 have 뒤에 올 수 없음
④ to wonder ❌ — to부정사는 have 뒤에 올 수 없음
⑤ wonders ❌ — 3인칭 단수형은 have 뒤에 올 수 없음
det.tip:
💡 현재완료 = have/has + p.p.
• 경험: Have you ever been to Paris?
• 완료: I have just finished.

⚠️ have 뒤에 동사원형/V-ing 올 수 없음!

det.correct: (A) find + O + p.p.(수동): be engaged in의 관계. (B) such as + V-ing: 전치사 뒤 동명사.
wrongs: ② ❌ — purchase는 동사원형이라 전치사 such as 뒤에 부적절
③ ❌ — engaging은 능동이나 be engaged in이 관용적
⑤ ❌ — purchased는 과거분사로 동명사 자리에 부적절
det.tip:
💡 find + O + OC
• find + O + p.p. (수동)
• find + O + V-ing (능동/진행)
• such as 뒤에는 명사/동명사

questions.stem:

[해석] 경제 상황이 유리하다. 그것들에는 높은 고용률, GDP 증가가 포함된다. [문장 32~33 참고]
det.correct: They는 앞 문장의 economic conditions를 가리킴. 경제 상황의 구체적 내용을 나열.
wrongs: ① ❌ — bull markets는 단수 개념으로 다뤄짐
⑤ ❌ — employment rates는 They에 포함되는 항목
det.tip:
💡 They가 가리키는 것
• 바로 앞 문장의 복수 명사 확인
• 내용적 일관성 점검

questions.passage: To put it simply, owning one stock is like <u>having a slice of the company's pie</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "having a slice of the company's pie"의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] owning one stock is like having a slice of the company's pie
[해석] 주식 하나를 소유하는 것은 회사 파이의 한 조각을 가지는 것과 같다 [문장 11 참고]
det.correct: 파이 한 조각 = 회사의 일부분 소유. 비유적으로 부분 소유를 의미한다.
wrongs: ① ❌ — 실제 디저트가 아닌 비유적 표현
④ ❌ — 돈을 잃는 것이 아닌 소유의 비유
⑤ ❌ — 전체 경영이 아닌 일부 소유
det.tip:
💡 비유적 표현 해석
• "a slice of the pie" = 몫, 지분, 일부분
• 실제 파이가 아닌 소유 지분의 비유

ch: ① eating a dessert at a company event
② owning a small part of the company
③ baking a pie for the company's employees
④ losing money by investing in the company
⑤ managing the entire company alone

questions.passage: In a bull market, investors often believe in the market's present and future ( ___ ). [perform]
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 11자, p로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] investors often believe in the market's present and future performance
[해석] 투자자들은 시장의 현재와 미래 실적을 믿는다 [문장 35 참고]
det.correct: 소유격(market's) + 형용사(present and future) 뒤에 명사가 필요. perform → performance.
det.tip:
💡 품사 변환: 동사 → 명사
• perform → performance (실적, 성과)
• appear → appearance
• allow → allowance

questions.stem:
다음 단어를 올바른 어순으로 배열한 것을 고르시오.
「a powerful tool / can / for building wealth / Investing / be」

det.ref:
[원문] Investing can be a powerful tool for building wealth
[해석] 투자는 부를 쌓는 강력한 도구가 될 수 있다 [문장 30 참고]
det.correct: 동명사 주어(Investing) + 조동사(can) + be + 보어(a powerful tool) + 전치사구(for building wealth)
wrongs: ① ✅ — S + 조동사 + be + C + 전치사구
⑤ ❌ — for building wealth가 주어에 붙어 의미 왜곡
det.tip:
💡 동명사 주어 문장 어순
• S(V-ing) + V + C + 수식어

ch: ① Investing can be a powerful tool for building wealth
② Can Investing be a powerful tool for building wealth
③ A powerful tool can be Investing for building wealth
④ For building wealth Investing can be a powerful tool
⑤ Investing for building wealth can be a powerful tool

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 영작하시오: "만약 투자를 하고 있다면, 돈을 잃을 준비가 되어 있어야 한다."
조건: must / be prepared to 포함
힌트: 1단어, 영문 4자, l로 시작하는 핵심 동사

det.ref:
[원문] But if you are investing, you must be prepared to lose money.
[해석] 하지만 투자를 하고 있다면, 돈을 잃을 준비가 되어 있어야 한다.
det.correct: be prepared to + 동사원형: "~할 준비가 되어 있다". 핵심 동사는 lose.
det.tip:
💡 be prepared to V
• must be prepared to lose money
• 투자의 위험성을 강조하는 표현

questions.passage: Just like other transactions, the prices of stocks are decided by the law of supply and demand.
questions.stem: 위 문장의 해석으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] Just like other transactions, the prices of stocks are decided by the law of supply and demand.
[해석] 다른 거래와 마찬가지로, 주식 가격은 수요와 공급의 법칙에 의해 결정된다. [문장 18 참고]
det.correct: Just like = ~와 마찬가지로, are decided by = ~에 의해 결정된다(수동태)
wrongs: ④ ❌ — just like의 오역, 전체 왜곡
det.tip:
💡 Just like = ~와 마찬가지로
• be decided by = ~에 의해 결정되다 (수동태)

ch: ① 다른 거래와 마찬가지로, 주식 가격은 수요와 공급의 법칙에 의해 결정된다.
② 다른 거래와 달리, 주식 가격은 수요와 공급의 법칙을 결정한다.
③ 다른 거래처럼, 주식 가격이 수요와 공급에 법칙을 부여한다.
④ 다른 거래를 좋아하듯이, 주식 가격은 공급 법칙에 의해 수요된다.
⑤ 다른 거래에서와 같이, 주식은 가격의 수요를 공급한다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: 이 글은 팟캐스트 형식으로 청소년을 대상으로 주식의 기본 개념, 주식시장의 역할, 주가에 영향을 미치는 요인, 투자 방법을 설명하고 있다.
det.correct: ③ 초보자를 위한 주식과 주식시장의 기본 개념. 글 전체가 주식 기초를 설명하는 교육적 내용.
wrongs: ① ❌ — 역사가 아닌 기본 개념 설명
② ❌ — 전문 트레이더 양성이 아닌 기초 교육
④ ❌ — 주가가 항상 오른다고 하지 않음
⑤ ❌ — 모든 위험 회피 방법은 언급하지 않음
det.tip:
💡 주제 파악: 글 전체의 핵심 메시지
• 반복적으로 나오는 키워드: stocks, stock market, basics

ch: ① the history of stock markets around the world
② how teenagers can become professional stock traders
③ basic concepts of stocks and the stock market for beginners
④ why stock prices always increase in the long run
⑤ the dangers of investing and how to avoid all risks

questions.stem: 다음 중 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.ref: 본문에서 Management is generally carried out by professional managers라고 명시. 주주가 직접 경영하지 않음.
det.correct: ① 불일치. 경영은 전문 경영인이 수행하며, 주주는 주주총회에서 의견을 제시할 뿐.
wrongs: ① ❌ (불일치) — 주주가 아닌 전문 경영인이 경영
④ ✅ — risk of loss and debt 명시됨
⑤ ✅ — bull market과 positive economic indicators 연결
det.tip:
💡 T/F 유형: 선택지를 본문과 정확히 대조
• "직접 경영" vs "전문 경영인이 수행"

ch: ① 주주는 직접 회사 경영에 참여한다.
② 주가는 수요와 공급의 법칙에 의해 결정된다.
③ 원자재 가격 상승은 주가 하락의 원인이 될 수 있다.
④ 주식 투자에는 손실의 위험이 있다.
⑤ 강세장은 긍정적인 경제 지표와 관련된다.

questions.stem:
다음 요약문의 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오.
A stock represents partial ( ___ ) of a company. Stock prices are influenced by supply and demand.

(1단어, 영문 9자, o로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] A stock is a partial share of ownership in a company.
[해석] 주식은 회사 소유권의 부분적 지분이다.
det.correct: A stock = partial ownership. 본문의 핵심 개념어 ownership이 정답.
det.tip:
💡 요약문 빈칸 채우기
• 본문의 핵심 키워드를 그대로 활용
• ownership = 소유권, 소유

questions.stem: 윗글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 내용은?

det.ref: 본문은 "there is a risk of loss and debt"라고 투자 위험성을 강조하며, 이익 보장은 언급하지 않음.
det.correct: ③ 추론 불가. 본문은 투자 위험성을 명시하며, 이익 보장을 어디에서도 언급하지 않음.
wrongs: ① 추론 가능 — 주식 구매로 부분 소유자 됨
② 추론 가능 — 고무 가격 예시로 설명
③ ❌ (추론 불가) — 이익 보장 언급 없음
④ 추론 가능 — public values 고려 명시
⑤ 추론 가능 — bull market과 positive indicators
det.tip:
💡 추론 불가 유형
• "반드시", "항상", "보장" 등 절대적 표현 주의

ch: ① 일반인도 주식을 통해 회사의 부분 소유자가 될 수 있다.
② 원자재 가격 상승은 기업의 주가에 부정적 영향을 줄 수 있다.
③ 주식 투자를 신중히 하면 반드시 이익을 보장받을 수 있다.
④ 오늘날 더 많은 사람들이 기업의 사회적 가치를 고려하여 주식을 구매한다.
⑤ 강세장은 긍정적인 경제 지표와 관련이 있다.

questions.stem:
다음 주제문의 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오.
An introduction to the basic ( ___ ) of stocks, factors affecting stock prices, and tips for investing.

(1단어, 영문 8자, c로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] let's start with the concept of a stock.
[해석] 주식의 개념부터 시작합시다.
det.correct: 본문이 주식의 기본 "개념(concepts)"을 소개하는 글이므로 concepts가 정답.
det.tip:
💡 주제 빈칸: 글 전체의 핵심어
• concept(개념)은 본문에서 직접 사용된 단어
